title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 133
paragraphs: The Greeks, then, sailed to Delos; and meanwhile Mardonius had been wintering in Thessaly. From there he sent round a man, a native of Europos named Mys, to the various oracles, charging him to go everywhere to consult them, wherever it was permitted to put the oracles to the test. What he wished to learn from the oracles when he gave this commission, I cannot say, for it is not reported; but I for my part suppose he sent to consult about his present affairs, not about other matters.
